title: Losing CO₂: Decarboxylation, Kolbe Electrolysis and Reduction
subject: Chemistry
objective: How the –COOH group itself changes: soda lime removes it as CO₂ (one carbon less), Kolbe electrolysis joins two alkyl groups, and LiAlH₄ or diborane reduces it to a primary alcohol, while NaBH₄ cannot.

fill.q: Soda lime is a mixture of NaOH and ____.
Sodium acetate heated with soda lime gives ____.
Kolbe electrolysis of sodium acetate gives ____.
LiAlH₄ reduces a carboxylic acid to a ____ alcohol.

tf.q: Decarboxylation with soda lime gives an alkane with one carbon less.
tf.explain: The carboxyl carbon leaves as CO₂.

tf.q: NaBH₄ reduces carboxylic acids to alcohols.
In Kolbe electrolysis the alkane forms at the cathode.

ar.a: Sodium butanoate gives propane with soda lime.
ar.r: One carbon is removed as CO₂.

ar.a: Kolbe electrolysis doubles the alkyl chain.
ar.r: Two alkyl radicals formed at the anode join.

num.q: How many carbons are in the alkane from Kolbe electrolysis of sodium acetate?

short.q: Write the anode reactions in the Kolbe electrolysis of sodium acetate.
short.solution: CH₃COO⁻ − e⁻ → CH₃COO·; CH₃COO· → CH₃· + CO₂; CH₃· + ·CH₃ → C₂H₆.
